graphEvents.label: What must the brief carry for a model to act on a command
Brief budget is 80 default and 120 ambiguous tokens
Doctor ids map to runnable strings; non-doctor ids do not
Recommendation payload has no kind or runnable field

label: The brief budget is 80 tokens by default and 120 when ambiguous, hard-capped at 120 with a 4-characters-per-token estimate; the fixed comment-hygiene directive block is appended after the capped head.

The actionable brief has one shape, Advisor: live; use <label> <confidence>/<uncertainty> pass., plus an optional Also: <doctor runnable> line; it carries no command kind, argument hint, run-or-ask verdict or undo class.
Doctor bridges render through a generated 35-entry id-to-runnable map, measured as /doctor:env list and /doctor:git hooks; this map is the only id-to-runnable translation in the renderer.

Non-doctor commands fall back to metadataSkillLabel or the raw bridge id; a literal /speckit:plan prompt produced the ambiguous brief naming command-spec-kit 0.82/0.20 against system-spec-kit 0.82/0.18.
The recommendation payload has skillId, score, confidence, uncertainty, dominantLane and status, plus optional workflowMode and routing diagnostics, but no kind, runnable or argumentHint field.

A model needs a runnable invocation string, a command-versus-skill discriminator, a run-or-ask verdict and a consequence or undo note; the current brief supplies only the label and two scores, and the doctor map proves the runnable-string part fits the budget when the data exists.

The budget is not the blocker: the measured ambiguous head is about 86 characters, the directive block about 205 characters and a generic command line under 40 characters, all inside the 480-character ambiguous budget.

direction: Raising the token cap as the fix
reason: The omission is a data-contract gap and the measured briefs fit inside the existing cap
